reason: occJSDM 0.3.1 fixed binary (one row per site) fits that attached covariates to the wrong sites when data$info$Site was not in sorted order; 0.3.2 makes the end-of-fit convergence summary linear in cost. The v0.3.0 pin carried the defect, which the server worked around by rejecting such data.

runtime.restore: r-runtime/restore-runtime.R into a new cloud-r-runtime from the CRAN repository and the retained occJSDM source cellar: 60 packages at lock versions in 510 seconds, 49 installed as CRAN macOS binaries and 11 built from source, occJSDM 0.3.2 among them. The development runtime r-runtime received copies of that bootstrap library and library.
runtime.local_toolchain_workarounds: MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 and a user Makevars adding the Homebrew gettext include path, as for v0.3.0. Local only; not needed on Linux.

lock_changes: occJSDM record only: 0.3.0 at the v0.3.0-beta commit -> 0.3.2 at the v0.3.2-beta commit; Config/roxygen2/version 8.0.0 -> 8.1.0 and RoxygenNote dropped, as in the package DESCRIPTION. Imports, Suggests and every other dependency pin are unchanged.
behaviour_changes_seen: Binary data whose Site column is not in sorted order are now accepted by validate_data and fit_model. The dispatcher's guard that rejected them is removed, and its own occupancy covariate preparation now mirrors runOccJSDM() 0.3.1: grouped by Site only for occupancy and two-stage data, used in input order for binary data. With the old grouping the validator's design rows disagreed with the fitted X_psi for all three unsorted test inputs; with the new one they agree exactly.
Binary fits now store the Site values in infos$siteNames instead of 1:n (1:n when info has no Site column). Nothing in the server reads siteNames; the reference driver now checks it.

Two-stage, occupancy and sorted-Site binary results are unchanged: every saved reference case that existed at v0.3.0 refits and passes its exact checks, and the dhole fit flags the same three parameters with the same R-hat and ESS values.

verification.native_reference_driver: 38 cases, 25 fits, 13 expected native errors, 128 of 128 checks passed. New: boundary_binary_unsorted_characterSite (FHT1..FHT40 in file order) and boundary_binary_shuffled_integerSite (a fixed permutation of 1:40) beside the existing reversed-integer case, which now fits instead of being rejected. For each of the three, six checks at tolerance 0 (1e-14 for the standardised covariate): X_psi equals the standardised covariate in input row order, X_psi and results_output equal those of the binary case with the same rows, seed and settings and no Site column, infos$OTU equals the input OTU, infos$siteNames equals Site, and the validator's preparation equals the fitted X_psi.
verification.pytest: 137 passed after test_full_native_fit_and_installed_source was updated from 19 to 22 audited reference cases (the first run failed only that count). The three unsorted-Site binary cases moved from the rejection test to the exact-agreement test, and a new test requires their reference checks to pass and validate_data to accept them with the expected design.
verification.acceptance: 19 of 19 cases through Client(module); 5 published fits and 5 tables audited exactly against direct native R

notes: Traits absent: native no-traits route retained.

workshop_dhole.timing_note: The laptop was on AC power, not in Low Power Mode, but busy with other work (load average 8 to 9). Direct runOccJSDM() fits of the same call took 20.2 s at ncores 1 and 13.3 s at ncores 2 in the same conditions, so the slower time than v0.3.0's 10.4 s is load, not the package.

workshop_dhole.agreement: The MCP fit equals direct runOccJSDM() with set.seed(2026) at ncores 1 and 2 (results_output identical, tolerance 0). Not compared with the workshop's saved dhole_fit.rds, which another session is regenerating.
